import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

### Research Summary: Top 7 Highest-Impact Task Beads to Work Right Now As researcher `gem` in this 5-researcher swarm, I have independently investigated the SASE project task backlog (comprising 1,427 total task beads, with 410 open and unblocked in `ready` status). The analysis cross-referenced active in-progress epics (such as CI contention repair in [`sase-1rq`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_15/AGENTS.md), update-skew handling in [`sase-1ra`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_15/AGENTS.md), and release train stabilization in [`sase-1s7`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_15/AGENTS.md)) to guarantee that none of the proposed beads collide with ongoing epic phases or duplicate active work. The complete research report has been written to: - **File**: [`next_seven_highest_impact_task_beads__gem.md`](file:///home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/sase-org/sase/sase_15/sase/repos/research/202611/next_seven_highest_impact_task_beads__gem.md) - **Snapshot Artifact Ref**: `file:explicit:e6831b39d8f44bf94ab58764` (`research:202611/next_seven_highest_impact_task_beads__gem.md`) --- ### Ranked List of the Next 7 Highest-Impact Task Beads | Rank | Bead ID | Task Type | Size | Core Subsystem | Summary Title & Primary Justification | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | | **1** | **`sase-1qm`** | `bug` | Large | Finalizers / Completion | **Host completion refuses an unchanged prepared-completion intent with `stale_worktree_fingerprint` after a passing check**
• *Justification*: Prepared completion (`sase monitor start -f`) is SASE's primary mechanism for zero-turn monitor landings. In this bug, a green 30-minute check (`just check`) is discarded at host evaluation time due to false-positive fingerprint divergence across linked repos, forcing unnecessary agent recovery turns and burning compute. Fixing this in `sase-core` restores automated completion reliability across the fleet. | | **2** | **`sase-1ot`** | `bug` | Large | Security / Compliance | **Rotate and purge the 27 historical secret-scanner hits in public `sase--agents` history (owner-approved remediation)**
• *Justification*: 27 secret scanner hits remain in the public commit graph of `sase--agents`. The repository owner already approved credential rotation and history rewriting via notification gate `custom-57bc7a62`. With approval already on record, executing this unowned bead immediately eliminates an active public security and compliance exposure. | | **3** | **`sase-1s4`** | `bug` | Large | Test Suite / VCS Integrity | **Find the test that leaves a stale lock in the real checkout**
• *Justification*: Observed in recent contention runs (`2026-11-08`), a test case escapes its sandbox and leaves an unowned `.git/index.lock` in the real repository checkout. This immediately wedges host-completion finalizers, `sase stitch create`, and all subsequent Git mutations in that workspace until manually recovered. Identifying the test and extending `_checkout_leak_guard.py` eliminates silent workspace wedging. | | **4** | **`sase-1s2`** | `bug` | Small | AXE Runtime / Teardown | **Runner module imports overwrite the process SIGTERM handler**
• *Justification*: Top-level module code in `src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner.py:87` and `mentor_runner.py:30` overwrites `signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, ...)`. Importing these modules causes pytest workers to ignore `SIGTERM`, causing hung tests, zombie `xdist` processes, and un-killable runners. This is a high-ROI quick fix (`small`) that removes a widespread test harness pollution vector. | | **5** | **`sase-1ce`** | `bug` | Small | ACE TUI / Prompt Safety | **Prompt `$EDITOR` temp file is deleted when the editor exits non-zero, losing typed prompt**
• *Justification*: In `src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agent_workflow/_editor.py`, if `$EDITOR` exits non-zero (e.g. `:cq`, syntax error, shell disconnect, killed process), the temporary file is unconditionally deleted in `finally`. Everything the user typed is permanently wiped out, directly violating SASE's core architectural guarantee: *"Never lose a user prompt"*. Preserving the buffer in prompt stash recovery restores prompt safety for human operators. | | **6** | **`sase-1db`** | `bug` | Medium | Storage / Data Privacy | **`attachments-private` store never verifies an existing remote is private before pushing attachment bytes**
• *Justification*: `preflight_sidecars` in `src/sase/sdd/_sidecar_init.py` only validates visibility if creating a brand-new remote. If an existing remote is public, SASE assumes it is private and pushes private attachment bytes to GitHub while the UI labels it `(private)`. Enforcing remote visibility checks prevents confidential attachment data leaks. | | **7** | **`sase-1re`** | `bug` | Medium | Scheduler / Bead Ownership | **Done monitor with stale `followup_pending` owns its bead forever**
• *Justification*: When a monitor turn finishes with `followup_pending=true` but the follow-up agent fails to spawn, `sase-core`'s stranded work classifier classifies the bead as actively owned by the monitor rather than `STRANDED`. ACE never alerts the user, the recovery reconciler never triggers, and downstream dependent agents remain parked forever. Fixing `owner_kind` unblocks abandoned bead lifecycles. | --- ### Implementation Sequencing Recommendation 1. **Wave 1 (Immediate Quick Wins - Day 1)**: `sase-1s2` (SIGTERM import side effect) and `sase-1ce` (editor prompt preservation). 2. **Wave 2 (Security & Privacy Hardening - Day 2)**: `sase-1ot` (purging 27 public secret hits) and `sase-1db` (remote privacy verification). 3. **Wave 3 (Completion & Fleet Reliability - Days 3-4)**: `sase-1qm` (prepared-completion worktree fingerprint fix), `sase-1s4` (checkout `.git/index.lock` leak attribution), and `sase-1re` (stranded monitor classifier).
